sum: Five or six days through Magar farming villages west of Ghorepani, staying in community lodges and homestays, to a hilltop at 3,300 m with a view from Dhaulagiri to Machhapuchhre.
reach: By tourist bus (7–9 hours) or by air (about 25 minutes).

guide.note: The upper part of the trail lies in the Annapurna Conservation Area, where the Nepal Tourism Board has required foreign trekkers to walk with a licensed guide since April 2023; checks on the trail are inconsistent. A guide is worth having here in any case: the paths are barely signposted, and someone needs to phone each village so the lodge knows you are coming.

access: Buses and jeeps run from Pokhara to Beni in about three hours, and Galeshwor is fifteen minutes further up the Jomsom road. The trail ends on the same road at Tiplyang, where you can flag down a bus or have a jeep meet you for the drive back.

photo.a: A line of snow peaks from Annapurna South to Machhapuchhre glows pale pink under a violet dusk sky, above forested ridges and low cloud.
photo.c: Annapurna South and Machhapuchhre at dusk from Mohare Danda

includes: porter in most packages (the cheapest tiers leave one out)
community lodge or homestay beds and three meals a day on the trek
bus or jeep between Pokhara and the trailheads

permits.name: Annapurna Conservation Area Permit
permits.where: Online at NTNC's e-permit site, or in person at the Tourist Service Centre in Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu, and the Nepal Tourism Board office in Pokhara. A permit issued at a trail checkpost costs double.

permits.name: Trekkers' Information Management System card
permits.where: Only through a registered trekking agency, which applies in the Nepal Tourism Board's online system with your route and your guide's details. Individual trekkers can no longer buy one over the counter.

transportText: Tourist bus between Kathmandu and Pokhara both ways
transportExtra: the local bus or jeep between Pokhara and the trailheads near Beni
tips: Book through the community lodge network or an agency so that each village knows you are coming; kitchens buy food for the number of guests expected.
Carry cash in small notes. Prices are fixed and posted, and nobody can change large notes.
Pack a sleeping bag liner and a warm jacket. Blankets are provided, but the rooms are unheated.
Ask before photographing people, and dress modestly in the villages.
Bring a refillable bottle and water treatment; most lodges do not sell bottled water.

days.t: Drive to Galeshwor, walk to Banskharka
days.note: Three to four hours by road from Pokhara through Beni. Cross the suspension bridge over the Kali Gandaki at Galeshwor and climb about 650 m on village paths, through terraces and orange groves, to the community lodge at Banskharka. It is hot work in the afternoon.

A day of steady climbing along the hillside through the hamlet of Dandakateri, on a mixture of farm tracks, stone steps and forest path, with Dhaulagiri in view to the north for much of it. Nangi's community lodge stands near the school; ask to be shown round.

The trail leaves the fields and climbs 1,000 m through oak, rhododendron and bamboo forest. There is no village on the way, so carry lunch and water. It is a big jump in sleeping height; go slowly and drink plenty. The lodge sits just below the top, which is at its best at sunset and dawn.
why: A climb of 1,000 m in one day, to sleep at 3,300 m. Go slowly, drink plenty, and say so if you get a headache.

days.t: Sunrise on Mohare Danda, down to Danda Kharka
days.note: Watch the sun come up on Dhaulagiri and the Annapurnas from the clearing above the lodge, then take a short, easy descent through rhododendron forest to the community lodge on the pasture at Danda Kharka. A restful afternoon after three days of climbing.
A forest descent, steep in places, that comes out above the stone houses of Tikot on a spur facing Dhaulagiri. Stay in the community homestay and spend the afternoon in the village.

days.t: Tikot to Tiplyang, drive to Pokhara
days.note: A sharp 1,200 m drop on stone steps and terrace paths to the Kali Gandaki road at Tiplyang. Buses from Tatopani and Jomsom pass through on their way to Beni and Pokhara, four to five hours away; a pre-booked jeep is quicker.
